subject: Energy
title: Chain Reactions and Criticality
description: A micro-lesson that makes Chain Reactions and Criticality usable.

hook.text: Criticality is the tipping point—where each fission triggers exactly one more fission on average.

buildup.text: Sub-critical means the reaction fades. Super-critical means it grows. Critical means it holds steady.

discovery.text: Reactors operate at criticality—control rods are inserted or withdrawn to keep the neutron balance precise.

twist.text: Enrico Fermi achieved the first controlled chain reaction in 1942—under a squash court at the University of Chicago.

climax.text: He sent a coded message: 'The Italian navigator has landed in the new world'—the nuclear age had begun.

punchline.text: One neutron per fission, perfectly balanced—that's criticality.

quiz.question: Where did Fermi achieve the first controlled chain reaction?
